summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and prior anoxic brain injury was readmitted for altered mental status three days after a previous discharge for similar concerns. Initial evaluation revealed a slightly elevated troponin, suggesting a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction, and persistent hiccups. Brain imaging showed no acute changes, with a stable finding in the left corona radiata likely representing a developmental venous anomaly. An esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed severe erosive esophagitis and an ulcer, prompting increased proton-pump inhibitor therapy. The patient experienced a seizure-like episode with bilateral contractions, leading to initiation of phenytoin, after which his mental status and hiccups resolved. His diabetes was stabilized with simplified insulin therapy using Lantus alone, and bowel regimen was optimized for gastroparesis-related constipation. He improved clinically, remained stable on new medications, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for neurology and primary care.
